Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:11:1.hebrew: יש ספרים שכתוב בהן מאי לאו ר' יהודה טעמא דנחום קא מפרש לא ר' יהודה טעמא דנפשיה קאמר - והכי פריך: מאי לאו ר' יהודה שמע לנחום דלא מחלק בעודן עליו בין א"ל "חמורך זה" בין א"ל "חמורך הוא", אלא לעולם קנה בעודן עליו, וא"ל ר' יהודה דיש הפרש? א"נ מפרש ממש, ולא פליגי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:11:1.english: There are books in which it is written: "What, is it not that Rabbi Yehuda is explaining the reasoning of Nachum?" [Or:] "No, Rabbi Yehuda is stating his own reasoning." - And this is how [the Gemara] asks: What, is it not that Rabbi Yehuda heard Nachum, who does not distinguish, while [the cloths] are still on it, between [a seller] who said to him "this donkey of yours" and one who said to him "your donkey [is here]" — but rather, [Nachum holds that] in any case [the buyer] acquired [them] while they are still on it — and [yet] Rabbi Yehuda said that there is a difference? Alternatively, [Nachum] is actually explaining [Rabbi Yehuda's words], and they do not disagree:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:1:1.hebrew: וכי תימא לרבנן ביטול מקח לית להו כו' - הוה מצי למיפרך מרישא דקתני: "אלו דברים שאין להם אונאה: העבדים והקרקעות כו'", מכלל דשאר דברים יש להן אונאה. אלא משום דהוי מצי לדחויי: הא מני? ר' יהודה היא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:1:1.english: "And if you say that according to the Rabbis there is no [law of] nullification of a sale, etc." - [The Gemara] could have raised a difficulty from the first clause of the Mishnah, which teaches: "These are the things that have no [law of] overcharge: slaves and real estate, etc." — which implies that other things do have [the law of] overcharge. But [it did not raise this] because [the Gemara] could have deflected [the difficulty] by saying: Whose [opinion] is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda's.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:2:1.hebrew: אבל בכדי שאין הדעת טועה [לא אימור] מתנה כו' - אומר ריב"ם: דליכא למיפרך מהכא לרב דאמר בפרק האשה (קדושין דף מו: ושם) גבי מקדש אחותו: אדם יודע שאין קדושין תופסין באחותו, וגמר ונתן לשם פקדון. דהתם אין המעשה קיים כל עיקר, אבל הכא לענין צמד המקח קיים, ואין סברא שמעות הצמד לא יחזיר, והמותר יחזיר. ומיהו האי שינוייא לא שייך באיזהו נשך (ב"מ דף סג:) גבי האי מאן דיזיף פשיטי מחבריה ואשכח יתירתא: אם בכדי שאין הדעת טועה לא צריך לאהדורי, אימור במתנה יהבה ניהליה. וי"ל דהתם ליכא למימר דפקדון הוא, שאינו יודע שיחזור וימנה אותם. ועוד, אפילו יודע, מסתמא כיון דלא הודיעו שהן יתירות אין דעתו לתבעו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:2:1.english: "But [where the discrepancy is] within the margin in which a person's mind does not err, [we do not say] it is a gift," etc. - Ribam says: One cannot challenge Rav from here, who said in the chapter Ha-Isha (Kiddushin 46b, there), regarding one who betroths his sister: A person knows that betrothal does not take effect with his sister, so he must have decided to give it for the sake of a deposit. For there, the act is not valid at all; but here, with regard to the fixed-price sale, it is valid, and it is not logical that he would not return the money of the fixed price but would return the surplus. However, this answer does not apply in [the chapter] Eizehu Neshekh (Bava Metzia 63b), regarding one who borrows [a number of] perutot from his fellow and finds an extra one: If it is within the margin in which a person's mind does not err, he need not return it; say that it was given to him as a gift. And one can answer that there we cannot say that it is a deposit, because he does not know that [the lender] will return and count them. Furthermore, even if he knows, presumably, since he did not inform him that they are extra, he does not intend to claim it:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:8:1.hebrew: אבל בשאין עודן עליו מודה להו נחום המדי - לרבנן דלא קנה. והיינו דוקא בשק ודיסקיא וכומני, אבל באוכף ומרדעת אפילו אין עודן עליו קנה, דתכסיסי דחמור הוו, וקני להו כל היכא דאיתנהו. ובקונט' לא פירש כן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:8:1.english: "But when they are no longer on it, Nachum HaMadi concedes to them" - to the Rabbis, that he did not acquire [them]. And this is specifically with a sack, a saddlebag, and a *kumni*; but with a saddle and a pad, even when they are no longer on it he acquired [them], because they are the donkey's accessories, and he acquires them wherever they are. And the *Kuntres* [commentary] did not explain it this way:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:8:2.hebrew: או דלמא בשאין עליו מחלוקת - ה"נ הוה מצי למימר: או דלמא בין בזו ובין בזו מחלוקת:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 78a:8:2.english: "Or perhaps [it is] where there is no dispute about it" - Likewise, [the Gemara] could have said: "Or perhaps there is a dispute both in this case and in that case."
